rationale: B wins because it turns the facts into sharper reporter-shaped business stories, especially "Ramp puts an AI agent to work on vendor contracts, but a human still hits send," which has a real governance beat and a concrete proof path. A has good instincts, but "Spend visibility alone didn't save these 200 companies" rests on "presumably," which is PR's quiet way of saying "we don't know." B still overreaches in spots, but it catches more of its own weak points and gives the founder better pre-pitch questions.
gaps_in_A: "As Ramp customers, this beta group presumably already had spend visibility" is the biggest foul. The update does not say the beta companies were existing Ramp customers or had prior spend visibility, so the whole contrarian angle is built on a guess.
"The average company wastes $342,000 a year" overgeneralizes a 200-company Ramp beta into a market-wide claim. It also blurs found savings versus realized savings.
"Ramp's new AI agent emails vendors" and "initiating a real-world business transaction" overstate autonomy. The given fact is that the agent drafts emails the finance team approves.

The next step jumps to "find-journalists" before resolving the median, sample selection, realized-versus-identified savings, and named-customer proof that several angles need to survive first contact.
gaps_in_B: "The AI agent's biggest savings didn't come from negotiating. They came from cancelling." The update says savings mostly came from unused seats and auto-renewals, not that cancellation beat negotiation. Good angle, premature headline.
"plans to charge enterprises later" is a stretch. The update says an enterprise tier with custom approval workflows is coming later this year; it does not explicitly say pricing or paid conversion.
"a human still hits send" is cleaner than the fact allows. The fact says finance approves the emails; it does not specify who or what sends them.
"attacks revenue lines vendors have quietly relied on" is a useful vendor-side frame, but it still needs a vendor response or contract example before it becomes more than a smart suspicion.
